subject.title: [Bug]: Feishu streaming card full-content updates cause severe latency regression on long replies

question: Should Feishu streaming cards gain an explicit opt-in append/compatibility mode for tenants where full-content CardKit updates are too slow, or should maintainers continue pursuing only full-content coalescing/pacing fixes?
rationale: The choice trades the documented full-content behavior and prior truncation fix against a live latency regression that appears tenant-dependent and not solved by the current coalescing PR.

options.title: Add Opt-In Compatibility Mode
options.body: Keep full-content as the default but sponsor a documented per-account or per-channel append/compat mode with warning text, regression tests, and live proof from an affected tenant.

options.title: Continue Full-Content Pacing Only
options.body: Reject append mode and require a different full-content batching, queueing, or CardKit request reduction fix with before/after live latency evidence.

options.title: Pause Linked PR
options.body: Leave the issue open but pause or close the coalescing PR until Feishu maintainers can reproduce the long-reply tail and decide the permanent contract.

recommendation.title: Add Opt-In Compatibility Mode
recommendation.body: Keep full-content as the default but sponsor a documented per-account or per-channel append/compat mode with warning text, regression tests, and live proof from an affected tenant.

likelyOwner.reason: The package metadata names this handle as the Feishu plugin community owner, and the decision is specific to Feishu channel behavior.
